# Mechanical construction 0.1.6

Pure SI queries: constructShaft(spec), constructHub(spec), analyseShaft(spec), meshForces(spec), screenRetention(spec), allocateReduction(spec), balancedReductionCandidates(spec). No DOM, storage, view state or dependencies. Actual gear/hub axial bounds belong to the geometry owner. Consumers submit those bounds, material limits, catalogue abutments, signed forces and editable construction dimensions.

Construction uses integral shoulders, removable stepped spacers, keys, end plates with axial M10 bolts, sleeves, covers, and one locating/one floating outer ring. Seal and cover envelopes are teaching dimensions unless a catalogue selection is supplied. Every component has a stable ID; assembly steps reference those IDs. Invalid passage or axial stacks are returned as failed checks, never certified for manufacture.

Beam: two radial supports, piecewise constant EI, signed point forces and couples in both planes, axial and torsional events. Reactions satisfy static equilibrium. Curvature is integrated exactly within each interval. Static von Mises at both sides of every section/load/keyway boundary; keyways use the conservative inscribed root circle and an explicit concentration factor. No fatigue, dynamics, contact pressure or bearing rating is inferred from this screening. Displacement extrema are sampled (81 stations plus all boundaries), not a certified continuous maximum.

Ratio allocation preserves driver tooth counts, rounds driven counts within declared limits, respects planetary assembly/divisibility constraints, and reports actual speed error. The consumer validates the complete native candidate before adoption.

Primary references: SKF Rolling Bearings 17000/1 EN, Bearing Maintenance Handbook 10001/1 EN; SKF Industrial Shaft Seals 18729 EN; MIT Roylance Mechanics of Materials (static beam elasticity); ISO 898-1 fastener property classes (Bossard technical tables); ISO 6194 seal interfaces. Numerical construction dimensions and concentration factors are labelled teaching assumptions, not prescribed by those references.

Validation: independent centre-load/overhung two-plane beam examples, keyway/axial section loss, torque balance, stack passage/contact identity, integer ratio allocation and consumer native round trip.

Nominal mesh-force cases use the mean bevel diameter and frictionless worm contact relations for conservative static screening. Axial force acts at the pitch radius, adding a bending couple. Direction/hand is a prescribed teaching load case, not a reversal/fatigue envelope. Hub axial extents use actual geometry bounds.

Gear-seat fit is supplied explicitly by the consumer. Spacer contact faces are checked against the catalogue inner-ring shoulder envelope. End retention reports separate bolt-proof, approximate thread-shear and annular-plate screens; the minimum governs.

Integral worms retain the thread-root diameter in the shaft profile and strength model, with explicit 5 mm end collars; the stock check includes their tooth-tip diameter. The gear surface owns the external thread.

Balanced reduction is an original teaching objective: minimise the largest pitch envelope with soft penalties for unequal cylindrical driven-wheel diameters and centre distances. It searches integer teeth and external ratios 1…8, respecting the declared speed tolerance, planetary assembly and selected pulley minimum. Current modules, pinions, helix angles and face widths are fixed. The result is a bounded candidate list; the consumer screens motor power, output torque, tooth strength and complete native input validity. It is not a global minimum-mass, fatigue or manufacturing optimisation. For two cylindrical stages an independent equal-wheel-diameter starting estimate is u1 = sqrt(uReducer * (m2*z12/cos(beta2))/(m1*z11/cos(beta1))).

`recommendedRatioSpans` gives soft starting spans, with explicit deviations on each candidate. Reference: D. O. Mishchuk, V. P. Rashkivskyi, *Systems of automated design in mechanical engineering*, Kyiv: KNUBA, 2016, p.14 table 4, https://library.knuba.edu.ua/books/17_3_16.pdf. Enclosed gears 3…6, chain 2…6, normal belts ≤4, one-start worms 28…80 and two-start worms 14…40. The wider cylindrical 2…8, bevel 2…5, synchronous-belt 2…6, planetary 3…8 and four-start-worm 8…20 spans are teaching search assumptions, not quoted standard limits. Candidates inside all spans are preferred, then geometry ranks them. When none is inside, a weighted logarithmic penalty discourages departures; it never changes the requested speed or silently rejects a feasible manual split. Worm stages are not forced toward equal wheel diameters with cylindrical stages. An impossible combination remains explicitly outside the advice instead of receiving fabricated tooth counts.

Planetary allocation is fixed ring, sun input, carrier output: u = 1 + zRing/zSun, zRing = zSun + 2*zPlanet. Equal-spacing assembly and adjacent planet tip clearance are checked for every candidate. Pitch diameter and envelope diameter are separate: the nominal ring envelope is m*(zRing+2.5)+2*rimThickness, so the cavity roots and specified rim are both included.
